register_pressure.notes: Per window (16 tokens, C=32): qkv weights 32x96=3072 fp16, proj 32x32=1024, fc1 32x128=4096, fc2 128x32=4096, plus LN params. Per-window activations small (16x32=512, 16x128=2048). Full fusion per-window feasible if weights are loaded once or kept in shared memory.

nodes.notes: PROBLEM: Simplified Swin block fp16: LN -> W-MSA(4x4 window, 1 head, dim=32) -> residual -> LN -> MLP(32->128->32, GELU) -> residual. Input (1,720,1280,32). Windows: 180*320=57600 windows of N=16 tokens. CANONICAL: per-window independent (no shift). LN reduces over C=32. qkv: (16,32)x(32,96). attn: (16,32)x(32,16)+bias, softmax over 16, x(16,16)x(16,32). proj: (16,32)x(32,32). LN2 over 32. fc1 (16,32)x(32,128)+GELU. fc2 (16,128)x(128,32). LAYOUT: input NHWC contiguous; windows are non-contiguous spatial blocks (stride Wh,Ww). RPE bias broadcast across windows. REGIMES: (a) bandwidth-bound elementwise/LN — need fusion; (b) tiny GEMMs latency-bound — need to batch many windows per CTA; (c) softmax+attention compute small but many launches. KNOBS: per-CTA window count, weight staging (shared vs reload), fuse LN+QKV, fuse softmax+attn@V+proj, fuse LN2+fc1+GELU+fc2+residual, dtype of accumulation (fp32). FULL FUSION: per-window working set very small (~10KB activations + ~13KB weights fp16). Weights are SHARED across all windows → keep in shared memory loaded once per CTA, process many windows per CTA. Two big fused kernels: (K1) LN1+QKV+attn+proj+residual; (K2) LN2+fc1+GELU+fc2+residual. Possibly one mega-kernel. FAMILIES: F1 = two-mega-kernel fusion with multi-window per CTA, weights in shared; F2 = single mega-kernel everything; F3 = persistent CTA over windows with weights in registers. Top pick: F1 (manageable register pressure, full fusion of memory traffic). SELF_CHECK note: families differ in fusion scope and weight residency.

action.description: Implement two fused Triton kernels. Kernel A: per-window load NHWC slice, fused LayerNorm1 + QKV linear (via tl.dot with weight tile in shared) + scaled dot-product attention (16x16) + RPE add + softmax (fp32 accum) + attn@V + proj linear + residual add, writing back to NHWC. Kernel B: fused LayerNorm2 + fc1 (32->128) + GELU + fc2 (128->32) + residual. Each CTA processes BLOCK_W windows (e.g., 4-16). Weights loaded once per CTA into shared memory; biases/LN params in registers.
action.rationale: Reduces HBM traffic from ~10+ passes over the activation tensor to 2 passes. Tensor cores via tl.dot for the GEMMs. Many windows per CTA amortizes weight loads.
action.title: Two fused mega-kernels: (LN1+Attn+Proj+Res) and (LN2+MLP+Res)

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin transformer block in fp16 on (1,720,1280,32) input with 4x4 non-shifted windows, single head, dim=32, MLP hidden=128. Computation per 16-token window is independent: LN1 → QKV linear → scaled QK^T + RPE bias → softmax → attn·V → proj → residual → LN2 → fc1 → GELU → fc2 → residual. Tensors are small (16x32 per window), weights are tiny (~12KB total) and shared across all 57,600 windows, making this a bandwidth-bound problem that benefits enormously from full operator fusion to avoid repeated HBM round-trips of the 58MB activation. Key constraints: NHWC layout with window gather, tl.dot minimum tile 16x16x16 (fits), fp32 accumulation for softmax/LN stability, RPE bias broadcast across windows. Target: 2 fused mega-kernels (attention block, MLP block) processing multiple windows per CTA with weights staged in shared memory.
open_questions: Optimal BLOCK_W (windows per CTA) trading register pressure vs tensor-core utilization — likely 4–16.
Should weights live in shared memory (loaded once per CTA) or be re-broadcast via tl.load each iteration?
Is window gather from NHWC efficient via direct indexing, or should we pre-permute input to (num_windows, 16, 32) once?
Does a single mega-kernel fit in registers without spilling, or must we split at the residual boundary?
How to handle the residual add correctness when fusing — need to keep original fp16 input in registers across the whole pipeline.
Can we use tl.dot for the 16x16 QK^T or is a manual reduction faster given the tiny K=32?
Numerical tolerance for softmax in fp16 — accumulate in fp32 and ensure LN matches PyTorch's fp32-accumulating fp16 LN.
